clue.text: Top decoration's worn by brass hat at breakfast?

definitions.text: Top decoration's worn by brass hat at breakfast?

parts.words: Top decoration's worn by brass hat
parts.note: surface reading: a senior officer pins some medal or badge on top while eating his morning meal
setter's reading: the gold braid on a senior officer's cap peak has a slang name that is also a breakfast dish of beaten, cooked eggs

explanation.surface: A senior officer turns up to breakfast wearing his decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: A brass hat is a high-ranking officer; the gold oak-leaf braid on his cap peak is nicknamed SCRAMBLED EGGS, which is also what he might eat at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Military slang names the gold cap-peak braid after the breakfast dish, so one phrase covers both the uniform trimming and the meal.

clue.text: Robin's arboreal habitat

parts.note: surface reading: the small red-breasted bird, which lives among trees
setter's reading: the outlaw Robin Hood, whose legendary home was a Nottinghamshire woodland

explanation.surface: A nature note about where the robin lives among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is a decoy: the Robin meant is Robin Hood, whose band lived in SHERWOOD FOREST in Nottinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend places the outlaw Robin Hood and his merry men living in this royal woodland near Nottingham.

clue.text: This way over the Berkshire Downs

definitions.text: This way over the Berkshire Downs

parts.note: surface reading: a pointer giving directions across the hills
setter's reading: put this word before 'way' and you get the name of the ancient track running along those hills

explanation.surface: A signpost pointing walkers across the Berkshire hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ridgeway is a prehistoric path along the chalk Berkshire Downs in southern England, so 'this' plus 'way' names it; the answer is the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow hilltop crest, and the ancient track follows exactly such a crest along the downland.

clue.text: As a southerner I remain old-fashioned

indicators.note: something fashioned has been shaped or made anew, so the preceding letters are worked into a different form

parts.note: all ten letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone from the south admits to being stuck in old ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' reads as one adjective, but 'old' belongs to the letters and only 'fashioned' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means an inhabitant of the south, especially of southern France.

clue.text: Attraction about end of work-time is this

definitions.text: Attraction about end of work-time is this

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for attraction wraps itself round what follows

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or enticement

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of the hyphenated phrase is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the phrase
taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle: what draws you in once the working day is over?
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion goes after the first letter of the attraction word, and then the whole sentence also describes the answer: the free time that comes once work ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time is the attraction that begins once the working day finishes, which is exactly what the whole sentence describes.

clue.text: Track about right for two- ' wheeler

parts.note: to dog someone is to track or follow them
ca is short for circa, Latin for about
a standard abbreviation of right

explanation.surface: Directions for laying out a race track suitable for a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' looks like a noun for a racecourse, but it is the verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogcart is a light horse-drawn carriage on two wheels, originally with a box for carrying sporting dogs.

clue.text: Navy's extra cut

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in Royal Navy slang, spare or surplus, anything going free
second meaning: a deep wound or slash

explanation.surface: The navy takes an extra share of the cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Naval slang uses the word for spare or leftover food and goods, which is the sense 'extra' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call anything spare or surplus by this word, and in everyday English it is a long deep cut or wound.

clue.text: Play made in France, I hear

parts.note: first meaning: a drama by George Bernard Shaw

indicators.note: what someone hears is spoken, so a word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: second meaning, heard: the Maid of Orleans, the French heroine later canonised

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a stage play was produced in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'made' is 'maid': Joan of Arc, the Maid of Orleans, was made a saint in 1920, and Shaw wrote a play about her.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's 1923 drama is named after the French peasant girl who led armies and was canonised by the Church.

clue.text: Hand's tribute .to the " Cutty Sark " ?

parts.note: surface reading: a crew member's salute to the famous tea clipper
setter's reading: a cutty sark is Scots for a short shirt or shift, and a hand is a worker such as a seamstress

explanation.surface: A sailor pays homage to the famous clipper ship Cutty Sark.
explanation.walkthrough: In Burns, a cutty sark is a short chemise; Thomas Hood's 1843 poem THE SONG OF THE SHIRT voices a poor seamstress, a hand, stitching shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood's poem is a working seamstress's lament over shirts, so it is literally verse in honour of a short Scottish garment.

clue.text: Backing objective with gold — sign of change

indicators.note: a word subject to change can be altered, so its letters are moved into another order

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective
or is gold in heraldry
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A financial note about supporting a goal with gold as a signal that things are shifting.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold is a heraldic convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorsing a candidate or plan means giving it public support, the same as backing it.

clue.text: For part of Ireland soil analysis holds key

indicators.note: analysis breaks something down into its parts, which can then be put back in a new order
to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
G is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Testing the soil in an Irish region turns out to be crucial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as an adjective meaning crucial, but it is a musical key, one of the letters A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county and town in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Hold and use a part of Kent, say

indicators.note: say asks you to speak the phrase, so it is matched by how it sounds

parts.note: the Weald is a once-wooded region of Kent and Sussex

explanation.surface: A landowner keeps and farms a stretch of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weald is the area of south-east England between the North and South Downs, much of it in the county of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To wield a tool or power is to grip it and put it to work, so both holding and using are covered.

clue.text: Upstart god returns to the mountains

parts.note: split as 'up start': the start of the word up

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Lar is a Roman household god, plural Lares

explanation.surface: An upstart deity heads back to his mountain home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstart' looks like one word for a social climber, but read it as 'up start', the opening letter of 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urals are the range dividing European from Asian Russia, often called simply the mountains of that name.

clue.text: Party man a Stock Exchange speculator

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a man at an all-male party held before a wedding
second meaning: someone who applies for new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit

explanation.surface: A political party member who also gambles on the markets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party man' suggests a political loyalist, but the party is the bridegroom's last night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Men attending a bachelor celebration share this name, and in City jargon it describes a buyer of new issues who sells immediately for gain.

clue.text: Snakes were legendary tree-dwellers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: king cobras, which carry this name
second meaning: wood nymphs of Greek myth, each living in a particular tree

explanation.surface: A claim that serpents once lived in the trees of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the king cobra of India and the Greek nymphs whose lives were bound to their trees.

clue.text: Landed from the sca

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on dry land, having come ashore
second meaning (the printed 'sca' is a misprint of 'sea'): blowing towards the land, as a breeze does

explanation.surface: Someone has just come ashore off the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the one used of winds: an onshore breeze blows in off the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes being on the land rather than afloat, and a wind that blows in towards the coast off the water.

clue.text: To swindle USA Gas Company I must be shrewd

indicators.note: to swindle is to cheat or con, so the following letters are twisted out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the usual abbreviation for company
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fraudster reflects that cheating an American gas firm takes brains.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone with keen practical judgment, quick to see what is to their advantage.

clue.text: Dash away for The Listener — swell cover

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap round it, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: a swell is an old word for a smartly dressed upper-class man
the ear is the part that listens

explanation.surface: A note about rushing off to fetch a copy of The Listener magazine, with its swell cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC weekly magazine, so it reads as a title; here it is simply the organ that hears. A swell is dated slang for a posh, well-dressed man.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear off is to rush away at great speed, the same as dashing off in a hurry.

clue.text: Terrible golf? A member makes light of it

indicators.note: something terrible is badly done, so these letters come out in a mangled order

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
taken as written
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician shrugs off a dreadful round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes light of it' reads as an idiom for shrugging off; only 'light' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fog lamp is a vehicle's lamp built to shine through mist, so it is one kind of light.

clue.text: Garment of light kid

parts.note: pale means light in colour
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing made of light kid leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like goatskin leather for the garment, but it is a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose outer coat or overcoat, worn by men and women in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Sturdy stem

definitions.meaning: first meaning: firm, loyal and dependable
second meaning: to stop a flow, especially of blood, as a verb

explanation.surface: A description of a strong plant stalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stem' reads as a noun for a stalk, but it is the verb meaning to check a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means firm and steadfast; as a verb, a variant of stanch, it means to halt bleeding.

clue.text: Measures concerning issue of a previous alliance

parts.note: steps are measures taken to achieve something
on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: Policy steps dealing with an issue left over from an earlier treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' and 'alliance' suggest politics; here issue means offspring and the alliance is an earlier marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a spouse's son from an earlier marriage, so he is offspring of that former union.

clue.text: Coast here is not necessarily ruined

definitions.text: Coast here is not necessarily ruined

parts.note: surface reading: a stretch of shoreline that is not spoiled
setter's reading: in the name of a Central American country, its Spanish second word means wealthy, the opposite of ruined

explanation.surface: A stretch of coastline that may not have been spoilt after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Costa Rica is Spanish for 'rich coast', so the word partnering 'coast' there translates as RICH, and being rich means not being financially ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy people are the opposite of the bankrupt, so someone well off is certainly not ruined.

clue.text: Light its solution ?

parts.note: surface reading: an illumination, or something easy to solve
setter's reading: in crossword jargon a light is an entry in the grid, which is the answer to the thing you are reading now

explanation.surface: A puzzle remark about light being the answer to something.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters call each grid entry a light; the thing whose solution goes into a light is the hint you are reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Every entry in the grid is the solution to a hint printed beside it, so a light answers one.

clue.text: Commits to paper sound forms of procedure

indicators.note: sound tells you to judge the word by how it is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: commits to paper means puts down in writing

explanation.surface: Someone records sensible rules of procedure on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as an adjective meaning reliable; it is the signal to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites are the set ceremonies or prescribed forms followed in a religious or formal procedure.

clue.text: Broken Petri dish

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of the next word are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cracked glass dish from the laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petri dish' is a lab phrase, but 'dish' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe, the stomach lining of cattle, is cooked and served as a meal, so it is a dish.

clue.text: Set sights on producing a cipher
Mark the double-cross

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a scratch or notch cut in a surface
second meaning: two Roman tens, written as two crosses, make twenty

explanation.surface: Point out the person who betrayed you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double-cross' reads as betrayal, but X is the Roman ten, so XX is twenty, which is a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a cut line or notch on a surface, and it is also the number twenty.

clue.text: Conductor of opera gets point in one

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera
N, for north, is a compass point
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A conductor of opera scores a goal in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it sets one piece inside another, but it is simply its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian orchestral and operatic conductor who led La Scala and the NBC Symphony.

clue.text: Laconic form of Ted's hot answer

indicators.note: a new form of something is a reshaping, so the following letters take a different arrangement

parts.note: every letter of these three words

explanation.surface: Ted gives a fiery, brief reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A laconic remark uses very few words, which is what a brief and to-the-point reply does.
